    # Separator rows and columns divide the grid into nine panels. Encode
    # a panel with 3 for one marker and 1 for two markers.
    rows = [i for i, row in enumerate(grid) if all(v == 3 for v in row)]
    cols = [j for j in range(len(grid[0])) if all(row[j] == 3 for row in grid)]
    rparts = _parts(len(grid), rows)
    cparts = _parts(len(grid[0]), cols)
    return [[3 if sum(grid[r][c] == 5 for r in rs for c in cs) == 1 else 1
             for cs in cparts] for rs in rparts]

def _parts(n, separators):
    cuts = [-1] + separators + [n]
    return [list(range(cuts[i] + 1, cuts[i+1])) for i in range(len(cuts)-1)
            if cuts[i+1] > cuts[i] + 1]

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    rowcuts = [r for r in range(h) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1]
    colcuts = [c for c in range(w) if len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1]
    rb = [-1] + rowcuts + [h]
    cb = [-1] + colcuts + [w]
    out = []
    for ri in range(len(rb)-1):
        r0,r1=rb[ri]+1,rb[ri+1]
        if r0>=r1: continue
        row=[]
        for ci in range(len(cb)-1):
            c0,c1=cb[ci]+1,cb[ci+1]
            if c0>=c1: continue
            vals=[grid[r][c] for r in range(r0,r1) for c in range(c0,c1)]
            # The panel's usual color is its most common value; 1 marks two anomalies.
            from collections import Counter
            counts=Counter(vals)
            common=counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
            anomalies=sum(v != common for v in vals)
            row.append(1 if anomalies == 2 else (3 if grid[rowcuts[0]][0] == 3 else 5))
        out.append(row)
    return out
PY
